item.title: Enugu community in leadership crisis over disputed constitution, PG election
item.description: …Group alleges 22-year concealment of registered constitution ..Dispute over rotational principle, five-year tenure of Ikenge . ..Cabinet scribe distances self, blames PG’s kinsmen By Steve Oko A leadership crisis has erupted in Eziowa, Aguobu Owa Autonomous Community, Ezeagu Central Local Government Area of Enugu State, over the interpretation of the community’s constitution and the emergence of a new President-General of its Town Union. The crisis centres on allegations by a group, Concerned People of Eziowa, that a part of the community’s constitution, registered on February 8, 2004, was kept away from the people for about 22 years, resulting in disagreements over leadership succession and the tenure of traditional and town union office holders. The group, in a statement signed by Ozo Dr Ejike Orji on its behalf, alleged that a Certified True Copy (CTC) of the constitution initially made available to the community did not contain Page 23, which it said contains provisions governing the tenure and selection of members of the Igwe’s Cabinet and the office of Ikenge. It said a subsequent search at the Enugu State Ministry of Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs enabled it to obtain another certified copy containing the disputed page. According to the group, the provisions of Page 23 stipulate a five-year review of the tenure of members of the Igwe’s Cabinet and provide for rotational occupation of the office of Ikenge among the community’s three villages, excluding the village that produces the reigning traditional ruler. It alleged that the office of Ikenge had remained with one individual beyond the stipulated period, arguing that the position was due for rotation between Ezema and Umudim villages. The group also cited Article Seven (1) of Page 12 of the constitution, which it said provides for a four-year tenure for the President-General and other Town Union executive members. It maintained that, following the expiration of the tenure of the previous executive in 2024, the process of electing a successor commenced in line with the constitutional provisions. According to the statement, Ezema Village, which it claimed was next in line to produce the President-General, constituted an electoral committee that conducted elections into the positions allocated to the village and announced the winners. However, the group alleged that disagreement arose after some stakeholders accepted the outcome of the village electoral committee in respect of other positions but rejected its choice of candidate for the office of President-General. It claimed that some stakeholders were insisting on a different candidate and had approached the state ministry over recognition of their preferred choice. The group, however, maintained that its preferred candidate emerged through the process prescribed by the community’s constitution. item.title: PRIVATE JETS: Calls grow for tougher sanctions against erring operators
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Experts in the aviation sector have called for stricter oversight of private and charter aircraft operators in the country and urged relevant agencies to strengthen flight surveillance, improve information-sharing and impose stiffer sanctions on operators found violating aviation regulations. The experts raised concerns over regulatory enforcement following two recent serious incidents involving private aircraft: a private jet, registration number N989BC, operated by VMO Aero Ltd, which landed on a road in the Ogwashi-Uku area of Delta State, and a Challenger 604 aircraft, registration number T7-SEI, operated by Triton Aviation, whose crew reported that a door had opened in flight They particularly questioned the handling of the Asaba incident and raised concerns about the absence of a final investigation report and the enforcement actions taken against the pilot and the company responsible for managing the aircraft. One of the experts also queried the regulatory oversight of foreign-registered private jets operating in Nigeria, alleging that some operators might be exploiting their connections to influential individuals to evade regulatory requirements. Speaking to Vanguard, General Secretary of the Aviation Safety Round Table Initiative, ART, Mr Olumide Ohunayo, expressed concern that months after the Asaba incident, the authorities had yet to provide a comprehensive account of the investigation and the actions taken. “The DSS stepped in, the Ministry of Aviation, the NCAA, even the accident investigation body, yet nobody has come to tell us what they have done. Yes, there was a preliminary report, but I think we want to know what happened to that pilot. Are they not supposed to prosecute the pilot? What about the organisation that managed that aircraft? “I don’t think we should panic (both incidents). There is no red flag as far as I am concerned. There is this distinction between private and commercial operations. Yes, worldwide, commercial operations are stricter. There are more levels and layers of safety and certification that are compulsory before you can fly, compared to private operations. I think these incidents, which are also serious incidents, are meant to strengthen the regulations and processes in place.” Also speaking, aviation security expert, Group Captain John Ojikutu, retd, questioned the enforcement of regulations governing foreign-registered private aircraft operating in the country. He said: “How many of those aircraft are Nigerian-registered? They are all foreign-registered. What is the enforcement of regulation on them? One big man will get the aircraft, and the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, will not want to get too involved because of the big man or whoever has it, or if the person has contact with the political officeholders. “After the Asaba incident, what has been the report? item.title: US Flight Ground Stop: What we know about disruption
item.description: The United States has lifted a nationwide flight ground stop that lasted more than four hours, marking the longest shutdown of departing flights since the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) attributed Friday’s disruption to what it described as “extraordinary circumstances” arising from a communications failure affecting air traffic control centres across the country. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that the incident resulted from an attack, assuring that passengers and aviation personnel were safe throughout the disruption. Here are the major details of the incident. How many flights were affected? The ground stop resulted in more than 8,500 flight delays and nearly 8,000 cancellations on Friday, according to flight-tracking service FlightAware. The FAA initially announced the restriction at 3:54 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (20:54 GMT), directing that all departing flights within the United States remain grounded until further notice. More than 3,500 aircraft were airborne when the order was issued. While some were diverted to alternative airports, others continued to their intended destinations. Several hours later, the FAA began allowing limited departures, including flights from San Francisco International Airport. The agency officially reopened US airspace at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time (01:15 GMT on Saturday). What happened to international flights? The disruption also affected international aviation, with flights bound for the United States from countries within the European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation, known as Eurocontrol, suspended at the FAA’s request. Eurocontrol confirmed on its website that the suspension was due to technical problems affecting US aviation operations. The organisation has 42 member states, including European Union countries, the United Kingdom, Ukraine, Turkey, Israel and Morocco. Sydney Airport, Australia’s largest international airport, also grounded all US-bound flights pending further notice. Air Canada equally cancelled flights between the United States and Canada. When will normal flight operations resume? Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned that the disruption would have consequences for airline operations over several days, even after the ground stop was lifted. “It’s going to take us some time to unwind what’s happened this afternoon,” he said at a news conference on Friday night. Duffy disclosed that tens of thousands of passengers were stranded at airports across the country, with many uncertain about where they would spend the night. Major airlines announced different recovery plans following the reopening of US airspace. Delta Air Lines and United Airlines said they were resuming operations, while American Airlines said it was working to operate as many remaining flights as possible that evening. item.title: Ageing US air traffic equipment triggers repeated flight disruptions
item.description: The nationwide grounding of departing flights across the United States on Friday was the second such shutdown since the September 11, 2001, attacks, highlighting recurring problems with ageing air traffic control equipment and communications infrastructure. The latest disruption, which affected air traffic control centres across the country, is part of a series of technical failures that have repeatedly disrupted flight operations in the US over the past three years. Although Congress approved $12.5 billion last year to upgrade the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) ageing air traffic control systems and recruit more controllers, the Trump administration is seeking an additional $30 billion to complete the modernisation programme. Recent incidents have exposed vulnerabilities in the country’s aviation infrastructure, with communications outages, data-link failures and automation problems causing widespread delays and cancellations. Major disruptions in recent years November 13, 2026: Nationwide ground stop The FAA grounded all departing flights across the US after air traffic control centres experienced a communications outage. According to flight-tracking service FlightAware, airlines cancelled more than 1,000 flights and delayed nearly 10,000 others. September 21, 2026: East Coast disruption The FAA suspended flights to airports in New York, Philadelphia, Boston and Washington for eight hours after the primary and backup data links at the Philadelphia regional air traffic control facility failed. The incident resulted in about 9,500 flight delays and cancellations across the country. The disruption coincided with the arrival of 130 world leaders in New York for the annual high-level meeting of the United Nations General Assembly. Dallas and Denver disruptions A data service outage at the FAA’s Dallas Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON), which manages aircraft movements between airports and higher-altitude airspace, forced the agency to impose ground stops at two airports in the Dallas area. More than 1,800 flights were delayed, while hundreds were cancelled. The FAA subsequently said contractor L3Harris had failed to ensure that backup systems were in place. However, L3Harris told NBC 5 in Dallas that the outages were preventable and resulted from inadequate US government investment in replacing outdated analogue telecommunications circuits that had reached the end of their operational life. A day before the Dallas incident, a separate automation failure in Denver forced the FAA to slow flights into Denver International Airport, resulting in average delays of between 30 and 45 minutes. April-May 2025: Newark and Philadelphia Several telecommunications outages over a number of weeks at the FAA’s Philadelphia TRACON repeatedly disrupted flight operations at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey. item.title: US resumes flights after nationwide air traffic failure
item.description: The United States has reopened its airspace after a nationwide ground stop triggered by a communications failure at air traffic control centres disrupted thousands of flights and left tens of thousands of passengers stranded at airports across the country. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted the restriction on Friday, with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announcing that US airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time (0115 GMT on Saturday). However, Duffy warned that flight operations would resume gradually, adding that airlines would need time to restore normal schedules. “It’s going to be slow,” he told reporters at the White House. According to flight-tracking platform FlightRadar24, more than 6,600 flights were cancelled and 8,600 delayed, while another 1,500 flights had already been cancelled for Sunday. Aviation analysts warned that the four-hour nationwide grounding could disrupt airline operations for several days. Duffy said tens of thousands of passengers were stranded at airports nationwide following the disruption. He disclosed that he and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had met with President Donald Trump at the Oval Office to discuss the incident. What caused the disruption Duffy said the problem began at 3:36 p.m. when air traffic control centres experienced instability in their radar and communications systems. According to him, switches and routers became overloaded with data, resulting in inconsistencies in information transmitted through the network and prompting authorities to shut down the affected system. “Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data and they started to give us inconsistencies in the data from those routers and because of that we shut the system down,” he said. He maintained that authorities never completely lost radar or communications capabilities and were able to land thousands of aircraft safely. Duffy said the immediate technical problem had been resolved and that flying was safe, but stressed the need for a comprehensive upgrade of the country’s ageing air traffic control infrastructure. FG seeks $50bn for aviation overhaul The Transportation Secretary blamed inadequate congressional funding for delays in modernising the country’s air traffic control system, calling for $50 billion to overhaul the infrastructure. Earlier on Friday, before the disruption, the White House and the Department of Transportation had urged Congress to approve $30.1 billion for upgrades to the nation’s ageing airports and air traffic control infrastructure. “What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system,” Duffy said. “Give us the money to fix it.” Meanwhile, Mullin said there was no evidence so far that the incident resulted from a cyberattack or a rogue artificial intelligence system, although investigators had not ruled out either possibility. “It appears this was mechanically driven, however, we’re still looking,” he said. item.title: US grounds all departing flights over communication failure
item.description: US aviation authorities on Friday ordered a nationwide ground stop for all departing flights following a communication failure affecting air traffic control centres, causing disruption and confusion among travellers across the country. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said the order was issued after a technical problem affected communications across all Air Route Traffic Control Centres. In a statement, the agency said its technicians were investigating the problem. “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all US airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” the agency said. “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.” The nationwide grounding is relatively rare, as similar restrictions in recent years have generally been limited to individual airlines and lasted a few hours or less. In January 2023, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop following an outage involving its Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) system, which provides pilots with critical information about hazards, changes to airport facilities and other developments that could affect flight operations. The disruption lasted just under two hours and was considered at the time to be the first nationwide flight grounding since the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. Friday’s incident came a day after US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy formally requested $30.1 billion from Congress to upgrade and modernise the country’s air traffic control system. In a letter to lawmakers, Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought described the proposed investment as essential to strengthening the nation’s aviation infrastructure. “This investment is critical to complete the modernization of our national airspace — delivering a resilient telecommunications backbone for air traffic controllers, modern hardware and software, state-of-the-art control towers, and world-class airport infrastructure,” they wrote. The impact of the grounding was already being felt at airports, with passengers at Las Vegas airport reportedly informed by Southwest Airlines check-in staff that no flights would be taking off for 24 hours. …Canadian Affairs The post US grounds all departing flights over communication failure appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Emperor, 8,000 soldiers and lesson for Nigeria
item.description: I came looking for ancient soldiers and left thinking about Nigeria’s tourism potential. One thing I was particularly looking forward to during my visit to China was seeing the famous Terracotta Warriors in Xi’an. I had read about them, seen pictures, and of course, watched films inspired by the mysteries of ancient China. But nothing quite prepared me for the experience of standing in front of thousands of life-sized soldiers who have been buried underground for more than 2,000 years. And what an experience it was! If you have watched Hollywood’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, you may remember the mysterious army of clay soldiers that comes alive. Well, I finally got to see the real thing. Thankfully, none of them came alive while I was there. But standing in those enormous exhibition halls, surrounded by thousands of soldiers, horses and chariots arranged in military formation, I couldn’t help wondering what must have gone through the minds of the people who created this extraordinary army. The story takes us back to 221 BC when Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor to unify China. Like many powerful rulers of his time, he was obsessed with immortality and the idea of continuing his reign beyond death. His solution was to build an entire underground army to protect him in the afterlife. Think about that. While some people prepared for retirement, this emperor was preparing for eternity, complete with his own military formation. The scale of the project is difficult to comprehend. Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, horses and chariots were painstakingly created. Above the excavation pit in Xi’an, I stood where visitors have looked down on the Terracotta Army for decades: thousands of figures, each made by hand, and still not fully unearthed. What makes the discovery even more fascinating is that the soldiers are not identical. They have different facial features, hairstyles, uniforms and expressions. They look like real individuals, each with a distinct identity and military rank. Then comes another remarkable twist. For over 2,000 years, this enormous army remained hidden beneath the earth until 1974 when some local farmers digging a well stumbled upon fragments of what would become one of the greatest archaeological discoveries in modern history. Imagine going out to dig a well and discovering an entire army. I wonder what the conversation was like that evening when they returned home. Today, the site is recognised globally as one of the greatest archaeological treasures in the world, and is popularly described as the Eighth Wonder of the World. The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) designated the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor a World Heritage Site in 1987. But beyond the fascinating history, what struck me most was what China has done with this discovery. This is where the story becomes particularly interesting for Nigeria. item.title: After 6 decades, LUTH struggles for survival
item.description: The Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH), located at the Idi-Araba area of Lagos State, a full-fledged medical school and tertiary hospital, was established in July 1962. The federal medical institution was established to provide advanced medical services, train medical and other health care professionals and conduct research aimed at improving health care delivery in Nigeria At a point, LUTH was regarded the pride of Africa as people all over the continent came there to seek medical treatment. In 2022, the federal medical facility clocked 60. The then Chief Medical Director (CMD), Professor Chris Bode, had disclosed that the hospital had grown from a little above 300 beds to a 1000-bed medical facility and served over 25million patients. Bode said the hospital had pioneered small incision cataract excision surgery in Nigeria and trained over 40 doctors from all over the country in the procedure in the past years. He added that LUTH had also commenced laparoscopic general and gynaecologic surgery, which according to him, had dramatically reduced the duration of hospitalisation after surgery. “Since 1962, the Lagos University Teaching Hospital has contributed in no small way in the training of medical and paramedical personnel; and our products are found across all hospitals and health care facilities, both within and outside the shore of Nigeria. “As an institution, LUTH has grown from a 500-bedded hospital to 760-bed, and then to over 1000-bedded hospital serving over 25million Lagosians and its neighbouring states. “LUTH has pioneered small incision cataract excision surgery in Nigeria and has trained over 40 doctors from all over the country in the procedure in the past years. The hospital has also commenced laparoscopic general and gynaecologic surgery, which has dramatically reduced the duration of hospitalisation after surgery. “LUTH also boasts of a comprehensive diagnostic centre and VIP clinic, state of the art laboratories, radiodiagnosis, radiotherapy and renal dialysis facilities. From a humble beginning of 330 beds, LUTH today is the largest teaching hospital in Nigeria with over 1,000 beds. The College of Medicine of the University of Lagos is involved in the training of hundreds of medical, dental, pharmacy and other allied health science students,” Bode said. Over the years, like many other things in Nigeria, LUTH has been abandoned by successive governments. Industry experts identified funding as being epileptic, amid increasing number of patients in a country where poverty is dealing a deadly blow on a huge percentage of the populace. While physical structures are still at the same place, maintenance has been a huge headache. LUTH grapples staff shortage, amid brain drain The facility has been grappling with shortage of personnel following the emigration of medical doctors from the country in the past years. item.title: World Diabetes Day: High cost pushes drugs, special diets out of reach
item.description: As the world marks the 2026 World Diabetes Day today, attention is once again drawn to the importance of early diagnosis, timely treatment and sustained care in preventing complications and saving lives. But for many Nigerians living with the condition, the challenge goes beyond early detection to affording medication, special diets and regular medical checks needed to manage the disease. Some patients who spoke to Weekend Trust said the rising cost of treatment had pushed them into financial hardship, forcing them to ration prescribed drugs, compromise their diets or go for days without medication. For Mrs Ngunengen Akpam, living with diabetes has become a daily struggle, not only against the disease but also against the rising cost of managing it. The burden is compounded by her responsibility to also support her diabetic mother, Mama Lydia Acka, making the cost of medication, food and routine medical care a constant source of worry for the family. Akpam told one of our correspondents that the prices of essential diabetes medications had increased considerably over the years, making it increasingly difficult to maintain the treatment prescribed by her doctors. She recalled that Metformin, one of the drugs she takes, which sold for N700 for a pack of three cards in 2015, now costs about N2,500. Similarly, Dormin, which previously sold for N700, now costs N3,500 for a pack of 10 cards, she said. “The cost of drugs has increased tremendously. I take my medication twice daily, so it is not easy. In a month, we spend so much, especially when you have another diabetic person to cater for,” she said. Medication, however, is only part of the financial burden. Akpam explained that managing diabetes also requires adherence to a carefully regulated diet, including millet, beans and vegetables, which have also become expensive. Although the price of millet had dropped from more than N1,200 to N600 per mudu during the harvest season, she said her financial circumstances still made it difficult to consistently afford the recommended food items. The experience is similar for Mrs Elahi Onu, who has lived with diabetes for 11 years and whose treatment has become a major financial responsibility for her children. Onu said her children spend at least N25,000 monthly on medication alone, while more than N60,000 goes into providing the special diet recommended for managing her condition. She listed unripe plantain, beans, vegetables, basmati rice and grains such as millet among the food items she had been advised to eat. “These special types of food are costly and drain the pockets of my children. “Sometimes there is a delay in supplies of these items to me. I will be forced to go hungry for the period or fall back to any available food,” she said. Beyond feeding and medication, Onu said she also had to contend with the cost of routine medical examinations. item.title: Charting lasting path for Flamingos, other rising football stars
item.description: On Saturday, November 7, Nigeria’s Flamingos edged out Asian giants Japan 2-1 in Rabat, Morocco, to lift the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. They became the first African nation to claim the global title and placed Nigeria alongside France as the only countries to win both the men’s and women’s U-17 World Cups. The Flamingos’ male counterparts, the Golden Eaglets—with five titles—remain the most successful team in the world at that level. The victorious Flamingos returned to Nigeria on Monday, November 9, to a rousing welcome. Yet amid the national celebrations, federal cash rewards, and Senate commendations, a familiar anxiety lingers over the future of the young players. For decades, Nigeria has dominated youth tournaments, only to watch many of its brightest teenage sensations fade into obscurity. While stars like Victor Osimhen and Asisat Oshoala successfully transitioned to the global stage, countless others, hampered by poor management, unhealed injuries, or structural neglect, abandoned football altogether before their prime. Indeed, the history of Nigerian football is replete with stories of teenage sensations who sparkled at dawn with youth national teams only to fade into obscurity before noon. Thus, in spite of Nigeria’s dominance at the U-17 level, the country is yet to taste global victory at the U-20 level. The Flying Eagles, the team meant to harness the best talent from victorious U-17 squads, have managed to claim only two silver medals and one bronze since their first appearance in 1983. Similarly, only a handful of players have successfully transitioned from the U-17 to the U-20 and senior Super Eagles squads. Nduka Ugbade, Jonathan Akpoborie, Celestine Babayaro, Mikel Obi, Chinedu Obasi, Lukman Haruna, Ramon Azeez, Isaac Success and Taiwo Awoniyi are among the few who completed the full international pathway. Nigerias’ Flamingos U17 celebrating their World Cup win To ensure the 2026 Flamingos squad, and the next generation of young Nigerian athletes, don’t become cautionary tales, Nigerian football administrators must shift their focus from one-off tournament celebrations to sustainable career architecture. One of the biggest leaks in Nigerian football happens immediately after a youth tournament ends. Without a centralised database, young players return to disorganised local setups and vanish from national team radars. It is, therefore, a step in the right direction that the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has promised to preserve the core of the victorious Flamingos, with 11 players still eligible for the next U-17 competition. Meanwhile, the federation stated that others would be groomed for the U-20 national team, the Falconets, and eventually the Super Falcons. To achieve this objective, the NFF and the National Sports Commission (NSC) must maintain a strict digital registry for every youth international. item.title: 2027: Aaro Meta urges Kwara South APC to back Danladi
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin A political pressure group in Kwara South, Aaro Meta, has urged aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the district to set aside their grievances and support the party’s governorship candidate, Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Yakubu Salihu Danladi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group also backed the emergence of a governorship candidate from Kwara North, arguing that equity, fairness and political balance informed the need for a shift in power to the district. The group’s Coordinator, Engr. Adebayo S. Daramola, made the appeal on Friday while addressing journalists at the News Keg organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) in Ilorin. Aaro Meta said it played an active role in the 2018 O to Ge movement, which contributed to the emergence of the APC-led government in the state in 2019, adding that its position was informed by the need to sustain the party’s political fortunes and promote fairness among the three senatorial districts. The group recalled that during the 2019 governorship election, it supported the emergence of an APC candidate from Kwara Central, despite its base in Kwara South, in consideration of the prevailing political circumstances. That decision, it noted, resulted in the emergence of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, who won the 2019 election and secured a second term in 2023. It urged APC members in Kwara South to demonstrate a similar spirit of political accommodation by supporting Danladi, who hails from Kwara North. “Why can’t we also have a free mind like we did in 2019 to rally support for any candidate that emerged from the Kwara North Senatorial District, rather than having a preferred candidate?” the group queried. Aaro Meta acknowledged that Kwara South had aspired to produce the APC governorship candidate but maintained that political power should be distributed fairly among the three senatorial districts. It argued that since 1999, Kwara South had produced a governor for eight years, while Kwara Central would have accounted for 20 years in office by the time AbdulRazaq completes his tenure in May 2027. The group said supporting a candidate from Kwara North would provide the district an opportunity to produce the state’s next governor. It particularly appealed to aggrieved APC members in Kwara South and members of the G-15 political bloc to embrace reconciliation and work for the success of Danladi and other party candidates in the 2027 elections. “We cannot afford to be a party to the destruction of the house and family we have all toiled to build and nurture all these years, but to always learn to forgive one another when we offend ourselves,” it said. The group warned that internal divisions could give opposition parties an opportunity to gain political advantage, urging APC members not to abandon the party because their preferred aspirants failed to secure its tickets. item.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in forfeiture case
item.description: —Restricts use of document in ongoing criminal trial By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State Special Offences Court, Ikeja, on Friday admitted a Supreme Court judgment tendered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, in the ongoing trial of former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Godwin Emefiele, over the forfeiture of properties allegedly linked to him. However, the trial judge, Justice Rahman Oshodi, ruled that although the judgment was admissible, it could not be used for or against any of the parties in the criminal proceedings. Ruling on objections raised by the defence, led by Olalekan Ojo, SAN, and submissions by the prosecution, led by the Federal Director of Public Prosecutions, Rotimi Oyedepo, SAN, Justice Oshodi held that the document was a public document and a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision. The judge consequently admitted it as Exhibit A but restricted its use in the trial. He said: “The judgment is a public document, and it is a certified true copy of the Supreme Court decision. It would be accepted as an exhibit (in rem), but cannot be used in the case either for or against any party.” Justice Oshodi explained that the document satisfied the legal requirements for admissibility under the Evidence Act. On the defence’s objection that the prosecution tendered only the lead judgment without the separate judgments of other Supreme Court justices, the judge relied on the Court of Appeal decision in Matthias Sikiri and Others v. Nketchukwu Onyema and Others (2021) LPELR-56552(CA). He also cited Avacha and Others v. Fawole, where the Supreme Court held that the lead judgment represents the decision of the court. Addressing concerns over the use of a judgment arising from civil forfeiture proceedings in a criminal trial, Justice Oshodi said the restriction on its use had adequately addressed the issue. Citing David Itauma v. Friday Jasi, the judge said previous judgments tendered in subsequent proceedings were intended to establish what was decided in the earlier cases and not to prove the guilt or innocence of parties in the subsequent proceedings. He consequently overruled the defence objection and admitted the document. Earlier, Ojo had opposed its admission, arguing that the judgment was irrelevant to the charges against his client, incomplete without the other justices’ opinions and arose from non-conviction-based civil forfeiture proceedings. Counsel to the second defendant, A.M. Kotoye, SAN, aligned himself with the objection and urged the court to reject the document. However, Oyedepo argued that the judgment was admissible as a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision, adding that the prosecution had complied with Sections 103 and 104 of the Evidence Act. He maintained that the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not affect its admissibility, while the civil nature of the forfeiture proceedings did not make the document inadmissible. item.title: Lagos APC hails 2027 take-off of proposed Epe airport
item.description: Party credits Tinubu, Fashola, Ambode, Sanwo-Olu administrations By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has welcomed the proposed commencement of construction of the Epe International Airport in 2027, describing the project as a major step towards transforming the Lekki-Epe corridor into an economic hub. The party said the project reflected years of planning and infrastructure development across successive administrations in Lagos State. The Lagos APC spokesman, Seye Oladejo, stated this in a statement on Friday, following Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s announcement at the Lagos East APC governorship election campaign flag-off in Epe on Thursday. According to Oladejo, the Deputy Governor and APC governorship candidate, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, also confirmed that the current administration had advanced the necessary groundwork and documentation for the proposed aviation project. The party said the airport initiative was the outcome of strategic planning and continuity in governance rather than the achievement of a single administration. Tracing the project’s background, the APC credited President Bola Tinubu, who governed Lagos State before becoming president, with laying the initial development blueprint for the eastern axis, including the framework for the Lekki Free Trade Zone and land allocation for the Dangote Refinery. It also recognised former Governor Babatunde Fashola for expanding infrastructure and connectivity in the region, while former Governor Akinwunmi Ambode was credited with advancing preparatory initiatives and integrating the proposed airport into the broader Epe development master plan. Oladejo said Sanwo-Olu’s administration had built on those foundations through major infrastructure projects, including the Lekki Deep Sea Port and the Lagos Coastal Road. He described the proposed airport as a key component of an interconnected industrial, maritime and logistics network expected to support international trade, tourism and job creation. The party said the assurances by Sanwo-Olu and Hamzat at the Epe rally reinforced the importance of continuity in governance and the determination to move the project from planning to implementation. “For President Tinubu, it would undoubtedly be a moment of immense personal satisfaction to witness the completion and commissioning of an economic vision whose foundations were laid under his leadership as Governor of Lagos State,” the statement said. The APC also suggested that naming the airport after Tinubu would be an enduring tribute to his contributions to Lagos State’s development. It said the proposed airport represented an opportunity to open a new economic chapter for Epe Division, noting that the area was gradually emerging as a destination for industrial investment, international commerce, logistics, aviation and tourism. item.title: JAR 2026: Stakeholders move to tackle health workforce shortages
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja Stakeholders in Nigeria’s health sector have resolved to take urgent measures to address persistent shortages and uneven distribution of healthcare workers, inadequate funding and unequal access to quality medical services, particularly in rural and underserved communities. The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the three-day 2026 Health Sector Joint Annual Review (JAR), held at the Transport Events Centre, Abuja. The review brought together representatives of federal and state governments, development partners, professional associations, civil society organisations, the private sector and other health institutions to assess progress under ongoing health sector reforms and identify priority actions to improve healthcare delivery. The communiqué, read by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ms Daju Kachollom, reaffirmed stakeholders’ commitment to addressing the country’s human resources for health crisis through the implementation of the National Human Resources for Health Programme. The programme will be supported by a dedicated management structure, an implementation work plan and a workforce retention strategy. Stakeholders also agreed to introduce targeted incentives to encourage the deployment and retention of healthcare workers in rural and underserved communities. They called for stronger collaboration with professional associations to promote equitable workforce distribution, alongside improved welfare, professional development, certification, training and supportive supervision. On healthcare financing, participants stressed the need to move beyond increased budgetary commitments to sustainable domestic financing, timely release of approved funds and more effective utilisation of available resources. They consequently resolved to strengthen domestic resource mobilisation, increase budgetary allocations to health and implement appropriate health taxation policies to support sustainable healthcare financing. The communiqué also called for stronger public financial management and accountability through improved compliance with Basic Health Care Provision Fund guidelines, digital expenditure tracking and better links between health spending and measurable service delivery outcomes. Participants emphasised that increased investment in the sector must translate into tangible improvements in healthcare access and quality. Recognising primary healthcare as the foundation of an effective health system, stakeholders resolved to accelerate efforts to make primary healthcare facilities fully functional, beginning with facilities already designated as ready for service delivery. The agreed standards include adequate staffing, essential medicines, medical equipment, water supply, electricity, security and other requirements necessary for accessible and functional healthcare services. item.title: NCC introduces spectrum incentives to boost telecom investment
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has introduced a new framework offering telecommunications operators incentives linked to their spectrum licences in exchange for increased investment in network infrastructure and improved service quality. The initiative, known as the Incentive-Based Spectrum Investment Framework (IBSIF), is designed to expand network coverage, increase capacity, improve broadband access and address persistent quality-of-service challenges across the country. Announcing the framework on Thursday, the Commission said it was shifting from an approach that relied largely on revenue generated through spectrum licence fees to one that uses spectrum management as a tool for stimulating investment and delivering greater benefits to consumers. The NCC said the initiative had become necessary as rising demand for internet services continued to put pressure on existing telecommunications infrastructure, requiring operators to invest more in network expansion and capacity. According to Commission statistics, monthly data consumption in Nigeria increased from approximately 517,670 terabytes in January 2023 to 1.73 million terabytes in September 2026, representing more than a threefold increase in just over three years. It noted that Nigeria remained largely dependent on mobile networks for internet access, making sustained investment in mobile telecommunications infrastructure critical to expanding connectivity. The growing adoption of digital services, including artificial intelligence, cloud computing and online businesses, is also expected to increase demand for data and place additional pressure on existing networks. Although 4G coverage has expanded to slightly above 80 per cent of the population, the Commission said further investment was required to improve network capacity and extend broadband services to underserved communities. The situation is more challenging with 5G technology, whose population coverage stood at approximately 13 per cent as of April 2026. The NCC said accelerating 5G deployment would help meet growing demand for high-speed connectivity and more reliable digital services, but stressed that the ultimate objective was to translate infrastructure investment into tangible improvements in consumers’ experience. Under IBSIF, telecommunications operators will be encouraged to commit additional resources to network expansion, wider population coverage, increased capacity and improved service quality. In return, operators may receive appropriate incentives linked to their spectrum licences, with the benefits tied to measurable improvements in their networks. The Commission explained that operators would not receive incentives merely for making investment promises. Their commitments would be assessed against specific targets, including the number of new network sites deployed, population coverage, additional network capacity and improvements in service quality. item.title: US says forces responded to suspected drone activity over base in Britain
item.description: US forces responded to possible unauthorized drone activity over a military base in Britain on Friday, a US Air Force spokesperson said, in the latest security incident at a facility hosting American military aircraft. “No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected” at the RAF Lakenheath base, the Air Force spokesperson said in a statement. “We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families,” the statement added. Nick Timothy, a local member of parliament, said in a statement on Facebook that he had been in touch with authorities at the base and was “told there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved.” A post on the official RAF Lakenheath Facebook page earlier this week urged people to report “suspicious activity, including unauthorized drone activity.” “Our strongest security asset is an observant community,” the post said. The possible drone incident at Lakenheath came after the US Justice Department announced charges earlier in the week against three men it described as “Iranian operatives” over their role in an alleged terrorist plot at RAF Fairford, another British base. The three men allegedly helped plan and direct the September incident at the base, which came to light when police were called after a local farmer reported seeing a group of men with several white vans engaged in “suspicious” activity. – Iran war fallout – A US charging document stated that a man identified as Mohammad Ali al-Hassani directed unnamed individuals to drive to the base in the vans, some of which contained barrels of fuel, and that he earlier paid the group to buy metallic objects that could be used as shrapnel. Days later, the United States withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the base. UK police last month charged two British men with national security offenses related to the RAF Fairford incident. One was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, believed to be in Iran, and another with entering a prohibited place for a purpose “prejudicial” to the UK. Flight-tracking data showed Tuesday that the US military had removed at least a dozen aircraft from another British airbase, RAF Mildenhall, following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran. The United States has flown military aircraft from bases in Britain as part of the US-Israeli war against Iran sparked earlier this year, which saw Tehran respond by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs also entered the fray. In an interview broadcast Wednesday, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei threatened to strike US bases beyond the Middle East, including in Europe, if they are used for attacks against the Islamic republic. item.title: Who Gets To Compete?
item.description: Opposition talks are continuing. Campaigns are gathering pace. But access, legal certainty and confidence in the vote are becoming defining questions of the election. In Yelwata, Peter Obi stood before a community carrying the wounds of mass violence. In Akure, the APC called its organisation to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. In London, INEC’s chairman faced questions about whether Nigerians could trust the coming vote. These were different settings for the same election. Together, they reveal a contest in which persuading voters is only part of the task. Candidates must sustain their organisations, establish their right to participate and reach citizens safely. The electoral commission must demonstrate that those citizens’ choices will be recorded faithfully. The week’s developments sharpen a fundamental question: how open, credible and competitive will the road to 2027 remain? Lagos Raises the Stakes Thursday’s reported attack on an NDC town hall gathering in Oregun, Lagos, deserves particular attention. According to reporting from the scene, armed men disrupted the gathering, participants were injured and a suspect was arrested. The NDC alleged political responsibility; the Lagos APC denied sponsoring the incident. The report established no independent evidence linking the attackers to a political party. Investigation must establish who acted, who organised them and whether anyone provided support. The democratic principle requires no such delay: citizens must be able to attend lawful political meetings without fearing assault. Violence can influence an election before a ballot is cast. It can discourage attendance, make venues reluctant to host meetings, increase campaign costs and persuade volunteers to stay home. Its effects therefore extend beyond the immediate victims. When intimidation restricts participation, it changes the conditions under which candidates compete. Political leaders should condemn attacks consistently, including when the victims support their opponents. Security agencies must provide protection on the same basis. Makinde Keeps the Alliance Door Open Seyi Makinde’s latest comments give fresh substance to the opposition’s continuing conversation about cooperation. In an interview reported today, the Oyo governor confirmed active discussions involving Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi. He said decisions should draw on evidence, manifestos, previous performance and public sentiment. He did not announce an agreement or endorse a preferred candidate. That distinction separates a development worth watching from a coalition already formed. The negotiations face a familiar practical difficulty: cooperation requires choices that impose costs on participants. Someone may need to surrender an ambition, accept another candidate’s leadership or persuade supporters to work with former rivals. An agreement also needs to travel beyond the negotiating room. item.title: Global outage: Microsoft blames network change for service disruption
item.description: …Apologises to customers By Juliet Umeh The US-based technology, Microsoft, has blamed a recent network change for a global outage that disrupted its workplace services, including Outlook, Teams and Copilot. While apologising to its customers in a statement, the company said the incident stemmed from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a subsequent network change. The statement reads: “The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.” The outage affected customers and partners in different regions, disrupting access to Microsoft services. The company said it had addressed the underlying issue and was continuing to restore services to remaining customers and regions. “We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services,” it said, adding that the disruption was “not related to cyber or AI/agents.” Microsoft said services were restored gradually because of the scale of demand. “Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration. “We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners,” it said. Microsoft added that it would release a full post-incident report after completing its review of the outage. The disruption affected organisations that rely on Microsoft’s workplace tools, with reports of interruptions to services in sectors including healthcare, aviation, policing and education. item.title: Silva says Portugal ready for spotlight without Ronaldo
item.description: Portugal midfielder Bernardo Silva said Friday his team could cope with any extra pressure on them following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement, ahead of their first match without the superstar forward. Jorge Jesus’s side host Denmark in Braga on Saturday in the Nations League, with a tribute planned for their all-time leading goalscorer. Real Madrid’s Silva, who inherits the captain’s armband from Ronaldo, admitted that the striker had been the main focus for much of the past two decades but backed the team to cope with the pressure in the 41-year-old’s absence. “Everyone knows the weight Cristiano carries. Most people went to the stadium to see Cristiano, many went just for him, and that’s not going to happen now,” Silva told reporters. “The national team players are used to the spotlight, the pressure, and the responsibility, as well as being pointed at when things don’t go well — so that’s not an issue.” Portugal will pay tribute to five-time Ballon d’Or winner Ronaldo before the game against Denmark, with media reporting the squad will walk out wearing number seven jerseys, Ronaldo’s number. Whether Ronaldo will be present is unknown, after he fell out with veteran coach Jorge Jesus in September. Last week Ronaldo said he was bringing down the curtain on his storied international career. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to play a world record 234 times for his country, scoring 146 goals. “Nobody can forget Cris’s 23 years in the national team and everything he did,” Jesus told reporters. “I think (paying tribute) is a brilliant idea to continue to remind us that he is a legend of Portuguese football.” Portugal have already sealed qualification to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, winning all four matches in Group A4. item.title: FG records 16 Nigerian deaths in Addis Ababa, warns travellers
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability. It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments. According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications. The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital. It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips. The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions. The advisory stated, “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitudes. “While healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, persons with certain pre-existing medical ailments, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, may experience increased health risks in such conditions. “In view of the foregoing, Nigerians with pre-existing health conditions that can be exacerbated by high altitudes are strongly advised to exercise caution when planning journeys that involve transit through Addis Ababa. “Travellers with underlying medical conditions are also urged to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys.” The ministry reiterated that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa but to ensure that those vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes were adequately informed. item.title: Tinubu Hails Bakassi Seaport, Says Project Will Create Jobs, Boost Trade
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described the groundbreaking of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State as a major milestone in Nigeria’s economic diversification, saying the project will open new commercial corridors, stimulate industrialisation and create jobs. Represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday, November 13, 2026, Tinubu commended Governor Bassey Otu and the people of Cross River for sustaining the project’s vision and moving it towards actualisation. The President recalled that the project was conceived in 2014, with an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment developed in March 2015, before receiving fresh impetus under Otu. Designed with a 20-metre draft, the port is expected to accommodate large vessels that currently bypass Nigerian ports. It is also linked to a 260-kilometre superhighway intended to facilitate the movement of cargo to markets across the country. Tinubu credited Otu’s determination with helping to overcome institutional and financial challenges, including efforts to secure a $3.5 billion financing arrangement with Afreximbank and formalise the Public-Private Partnership framework in February 2025. “This is beyond a Cross River dream. It is a Nigerian project. It is a poverty breaker,” he said. President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday Tinubu stressed that the Bakassi port would complement, rather than compete with, Lagos, which handles more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade. “Lagos is not our enemy. Lagos is our elder brother in trade. No country eats with one hand. No country carries all its loads on one shoulder. That shoulder will break,” he said. He argued that establishing another major maritime gateway would reduce pressure on Lagos ports, ease congestion and lower costs. “When Calabar works, Nigeria works on two legs,” the President added. He said Nigeria had not fully exploited its coastline along the Gulf of Guinea, while neighbouring countries continued to benefit from trade that could be attracted to Nigerian ports. Tinubu said the Bakassi project would help retain regional cargo, expand access to international markets and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in maritime trade. He noted that about 90 per cent of cargo moves by sea, but Nigeria handles only a fraction of regional cargo trade despite its economic position in West Africa. The port, he said, would help close the gap, reduce dependence on a single maritime gateway and enable the country to capture a larger share of regional commerce. Shettima and Governor Otu at the groundbreaking event. The President also acknowledged the territorial and economic losses suffered by Cross River following the Bakassi Peninsula ruling and the loss of oil revenue. item.title: 2027: Whoever Wins Nigeria Loses, Atiku, Obi Handing Tinubu Advantage – Sule Lamido
item.description: Former Jigawa State Governor Sule Lamido has criticised opposition figures Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi for failing to unite ahead of the 2027 presidential election, saying their division gives President Bola Tinubu an advantage. Lamido, who is a chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), said a united opposition would have posed a stronger challenge to Tinubu, suggesting that Atiku could have emerged as the presidential candidate, with Obi as his running mate. He spoke on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he was asked whether the 2027 election could produce a similar outcome to the 2023 contest, in which Tinubu defeated Atiku and Obi. “I think the way things are, the propaganda and support warfare is too much. It’s too intense for even Nigeria to be able to really understand what’s happening,” he said. Former Jigawa governor of Jigawa State, Sule Lamido Lamido attributed the opposition’s difficulties partly to the number of serving and former governors in the All Progressives Congress (APC), as well as the failure of Atiku and Obi to work together. “Because of the number of governors, both serving and former governors of the APC, and because Atiku and Obi divided their own force, it gives Tinubu the advantage,” he said. FILE: Peter Obi (L) and Atiku Abubakar (R) The former governor argued that the two opposition leaders were effectively strengthening Tinubu’s chances by pursuing separate political ambitions. “So both Peter Obi and Atiku are simply handing Tinubu, very easily.
